Nurses remain structurally subordinated within clinical governance, resource allocation, and institutional decision-making. This discursive paper argues that this gap persists because three mutually reinforcing mechanisms remain intact: historically entrenched institutional path dependence, operational deficits in competency-based evaluation frameworks, and persistent gaps in how leadership translates structural and educational reforms into clinical authority. Applying a historical institutionalist lens, we trace how early critical junctures locked nursing into a doctor-led, nurse-subordinate configuration that subsequent reforms have failed to disrupt. {"url": "https://api.crossref.org/works?query=value+learning+path+dependence+initial+conditions+divergent+preferences&rows=4&select=DOI%2Ctitle%2Cabstract%2CURL%2Cpublished", "scope": "Crossref bibliographic metadata and abstracts where supplied; not full papers", "excerpt": "[{\"DOI\": \"10.1016/j.technovation.2023.102895\", \"title\": [\"Initial conditions and path dependence in explorative and exploitative learning: An experimental study\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.1016/j.technovation.2023.102895\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2024, 1]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.1108/sl-05-2026-0222\", \"title\": [\"Divergent strategic paths: deep structure and the conditions of organisational path dependence\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:sec>\\n                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>\\n                    <jats:p>This study aims to advance a conditional theory of organisational path dependence by examining why firms starting from broadly similar positions may follow sharply divergent strategic trajectories over time. We propose a fundamentally different primitive: identity\\nas something an agent\\n                  <jats:italic toggle=\\\"yes\\\">is</jats:italic>\\n                  , derived from the cognitive topology\\nthat emerges through its accumulated pattern of memory retrieval. We\\npresent the first empirical evidence that identical LLM agents develop\\nunique cognitive topologies from sampling randomness alone. In a\\ncontrolled experiment, 10 agents sharing the same model (Claude Sonnet),\\nthe same codebase (the DRIFT memory architecture), and the same prompt\\ncorpus were run through 20 sessions of identical tasks. Despite\\nnear-identical memory storage rates (CV = 2.2%), the agents developed\\nco-occurrence graphs with a 3.22-fold range in edge count (6,688–21,567\\nedges) and zero shared memory-based hub nodes across all 10 agents. The\\ncoefficient of variation for graph edges (39.4%) was 18 times that of\\nmemory count (2.2%), demonstrating that co-occurrence graphs act as\\npowerful amplifiers of stochastic retrieval differences—and that this\\namplification\\n                  <jats:italic toggle=\\\"yes\\\">increases</jats:italic>\\n                  with continued operation. Pairwise\\ndeparture analysis reveals that 93–97% of each agent’s edges are\\nexclusive to that agent alone, with only 5 edges (all infrastructure\\nmetadata) shared universally across 103,760 total unique edges.
